name: Vegan Outreach: 2016 estimate (ACE)
summary: Encourages people to eat fewer animal products through leafleting, school visits, online ads, social media and mentoring. Animal Charity Evaluators' 2016 Guesstimate model: projected costs and achievements by program, converted here by species into chicken-equivalent pain days per dollar, like our other animal models: hens spared cages as hen-years of a caged hen's suffering, other animals spared with the shared figure per animal. ACE has since stopped publishing per-dollar estimates; this is the last public one for this charity.

sections.title: Model
sections.explainer:
Vegan Outreach provided budget and accomplishments information for 2015. Estimates in this sheet are made by Animal Charity Evaluators for 2015.

Read ACE's 2016 [review](https://animalcharityevaluators.org/research/charity-review/vegan-outreach/) of Vegan Outreach.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: charityevals adjustments on top of ACE's model.

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not ACE's. ACE's 2016 models count years of farmed-animal life spared, every species alike. Here hens spared cages count as years of a caged hen's suffering, and every other animal spared by the shared figure for an animal spared, split by species like a replaced meal. Each species is then counted in days of a chicken's disabling pain (Rethink Priorities' estimates); how a chicken compares with a person is the chicken slider.

rows.label: Schools visited
Leaflets distributed to the public
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 2500000 to 3335958 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

Vegan Outreach reported 3,012,700 booklets handed out (school and non-school venues combined), out of 3,335,958 booklets shipped to activists (including VO leafleting coordinators) in 2015. The total handed out could be higher or lower than reported, but probably not higher than the number shipped.

rows.label: Monthly engaged users (Facebook)
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 1030000 to 1401764 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

Vegan Outreach's Facebook reports show an average of 1201764 engaged users (anyone who clicks, comments on, shares, or reacts to the page) in a 28 day period. Estimated error due to variation over time is +/- 15%.

rows.label: Yearly unique video views to 95% (Facebook)
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 570000 to 770000 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

Vegan Outreach's Facebook reports show 330973 unique views to 95% over 180 days. This leads to our mean estimate of 661946 unique views to 95% per year, with error due to changes over time of +/- 15%.

rows.label: Years of increased retention per mentee
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, .083 to 7 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

We have very little understanding of the effects of Vegan Outreach's mentoring program, since they have not conducted extensive program evaluation on it nor are we aware of much relevant outside data. Since it involves potentially extensive personal contact between the mentor and mentee, we think it's unlikely to have on average a negligible effect (less than one month of additional retention), and could have a strong effect, up to [doubling](http://www.animalcharityevaluators.org/research/foundational-research/vegetarian-recidivism/) the amount of time mentees stay vegan.

Online ad clicks per dollar
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, .5 to 4 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

VO was unable to provide us with full outcomes data for their ads. For most campaigns, they were able to provide cost, ad reach (impressions) and number of off-site conversions (the behavior tracked on the ad landing page, such as clicks to order a Vegetarian Starter Guide). VO's campaigns appeared to be targeting a US audience, so we used this in combination with US data from another group providing ratios of impressions and conversions to ad clicks to find an approximate number of clicks per dollar for VO's campaigns.

SADs averted per animal spared
rows.explainer: The shared figures for a replaced meal, in suffering-adjusted days (SADs) and in animals, give the suffering behind each animal spared: about 8.7 SADs. Every model that counts animals spared uses this one rate, split by species. ACE's 2016 sheets don't give a species breakdown, so the split is ACE's 2024 estimate of which animals a plant-based diet spares.

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give: chickens
rows.explainer: The SADs for chickens with the hen weight built into the 2024 SADs ACE used (46% of a person's) taken out, which leaves days of a chicken's disabling pain. A chicken counts as 1 here by definition; how a chicken's suffering compares with a person's is the chicken slider. The evaluator view keeps Ambitious Impact's weight, so ACE's own result reproduces.
